clue.text: Sell famous footballer, divine in the middle

parts.note: Pelé, the Brazilian forward, is the most famous footballer of all
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, so a divine

explanation.surface: A club cashes in on a star player, with a clergyman brokering the deal in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle is to hawk goods, a synonym for selling them.

clue.text: One who has the will to get things dealt with

parts.words: One who has the will to get things dealt with
parts.note: seems to describe a determined person, but means someone holding a dead person's will, charged with carrying out its terms

explanation.surface: A go-getter with the determination to finish jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: This person is appointed in a testament to settle the deceased's estate, literally having the will to deal with.

clue.text: Member of conference was first to turn up, coming to eastern entrance

indicators.note: in a down light, turning up reads the word for leading from bottom to top

parts.note: to have been first is to have led
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone at a conference arrived first and turned up at the east entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is a representative sent to a conference or assembly.

clue.text: Flower comes with message about end of affair — very bad

parts.note: a river flows, so a flower is a river; the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: the message is placed around the letter that follows

parts.note: a cable is a telegram message

indicators.note: picks the last letter of the word affair

explanation.surface: A bouquet arrives with a note about the end of a romance, which is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' reads as a bloom but is crossword slang for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means utterly dreadful, a stronger synonym for very bad.

clue.text: Extend piece of writing provided by publicist

parts.note: a PR person is often called a pro
a tract is a short treatise or pamphlet

explanation.surface: A publicist supplies an article to lengthen something.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong or draw out in time.

clue.text: Like some fat pal involved with nature study carrying duck

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' shuffles PAL and NATURE STUDY to PLYUNSATURATED, and 'carrying' puts O inside after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain cooking oils and fats are described as having multiple unsaturated chemical bonds.

clue.text: Learner getting excellent name when taken in by elder?

indicators.note: says the pieces before are held inside the elder

parts.note: the elder is a kind of tree
A1 means first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: A young apprentice does well and is adopted by a senior figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elder' suggests an older person; here it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone being taught a job, a learner.

clue.text: Impressive building suffering harm, a lab

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is a celebrated Moorish palace and fortress in Granada, an example of grand architecture.

clue.text: Book, full of anger, beginning to seem tedious

indicators.note: the book holds the following letters inside

parts.note: a tome is a large book
ire is anger

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word seem

explanation.surface: A volume packed with rage starts to feel dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome and tedious are synonyms for boring or wearying.

clue.text: Repeated accident location in nursery rhyme? Fancy that!

indicators.note: tells us to write the location twice in a row

parts.note: in 'Ding Dong Bell' the pussy falls into the well

explanation.surface: An exclamation about where a rhyme's mishap keeps happening.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Ding, dong, bell, pussy's in the well' is a traditional English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubled exclamation of mild surprise, equivalent to 'fancy that'.

clue.text: Inside pub is the man who gets soaked?

indicators.note: says the word that follows goes within the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
taken as written

explanation.surface: Suggests the man in the pub who gets drenched with drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaked' suggests a drunkard in the pub; it is a swimmer getting wet.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer or someone taking a bath is literally soaked in water.

clue.text: Psychologist meeting German woman in the mountain

parts.note: Carl Jung, the Swiss psychologist
Frau is German for woman or wife

explanation.surface: A psychologist meets a German lady up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jungfrau is a famous peak in the Bernese Alps of Switzerland.

clue.text: Little people in air flying round to entertain me

indicators.note: means to host, so the reversed tune holds the next word
turning about, so the word for the tune is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
taken as written

explanation.surface: Small folk flit about the sky to amuse the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomes are small folkloric creatures, little people of legend.

clue.text: Awful beer's out, for certain

indicators.note: the letters are made a mess of and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Terrible beer has definitely been removed from the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish-flavoured idiom meaning certainly or indeed.

clue.text: Erudite drunk holding court? Goodness!

indicators.note: the jumbled letters keep the abbreviation inside
the word erudite is intoxicated and rearranged

explanation.surface: A learned man sozzled in a courtroom prompts an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness!' reads as an exclamation of surprise, but here it is the noun meaning virtue; 'drunk' makes REITUDE, which 'holding' splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectitude is moral uprightness, and goodness means virtue, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Some deer track heading west — something in the wood?

indicators.note: in an across light, going west means reading right to left
says only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: A deer's tracks lead west into the woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes EERT from 'deer track' and 'heading west' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is made of individual plants such as oak or beech, each one a woody plant.

clue.text: Deposits drunk in part of ship

indicators.note: the letters are tipsy and reeling, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stows away their savings while intoxicated aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The topsides are the parts of a vessel's hull above the waterline.

clue.text: Nurse finally meets doctor with fast car, an amorous type?

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word nurse

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
a racer is a racing car

explanation.surface: A nurse finally gets together with a doctor who has a sports car, a romantic sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hugs and holds others close, playfully suggesting an affectionate person.

clue.text: Europe's foremost expert returns, being invited

indicators.note: says the word for the expert is turned back

parts.note: a dab, as in dab hand, is an expert

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of Europe

explanation.surface: Europe's top specialist comes back after being asked.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is the past tense of bid, which can mean asked or summoned someone.

clue.text: Said to secure the possibility of adapting book for film legally

indicators.note: signals that a spoken phrase gives the letters entered

parts.words: to secure the possibility of adapting book for film
parts.note: a producer must purchase the film option, which is acquiring them

explanation.definitionFit: By rights means properly, according to what is lawful or just.

clue.text: Editor rising up, one who's spoken for rebelliousness

parts.note: a man who is engaged is spoken for

explanation.surface: An editor revolts, along with someone already engaged, out of defiance.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance, a synonym for rebelliousness.

clue.text: Where you may see Derby County, fortunate after losing start

indicators.note: puts the trimmed piece following the county

parts.note: Kent is an English county in the south-east

indicators.note: drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: lucky means fortunate

explanation.surface: Derby County seem lucky after a poor opening to a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby County' looks like the English football club; Derby belongs to the definition and County is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kentucky Derby is a famous horse race held annually in Louisville in this US state.

clue.text: Carrying on, top man secures English record

indicators.note: holds the following pieces safely inside

parts.note: a king is the man at the top
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: The boss locks away a British record and carries on.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping on with something means continuing or persisting with it.

clue.text: Loose stones, any number forming barrier

parts.note: scree is a mass of loose stones on a slope
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A heap of loose rocks piles up into a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is a partition or shield that blocks or separates.

clue.text: Something flowing endlessly — it is a nasal problem

indicators.note: says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a river flows; the Rhine is a European river
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something keeps running endlessly, which is a problem for the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something flowing endlessly' sounds like a runny nose; it is a river with its last letter lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinitis is inflammation of the mucous membrane inside the nose.

clue.text: Trick unfortunately enticed knight to come out

indicators.note: the remaining letters are put into a disordered arrangement
says the knight's letter is removed

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A ruse unluckily lured a knight into the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come out' removes N from ENTICED, leaving ETICED, which 'unfortunately' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceit is deception or trickery, so a trick is a noun sense of it.

clue.text: Poignant act of tactile person

definitions.meaning: a hands-on person keeps making physical contact

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both emotionally moving and the act of making physical contact.

clue.text: Surprising dangers eating cold meat

indicators.note: the shuffled letters consume the abbreviation
the letters are startled into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Unexpected hazards involve consuming chilled food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprising' turns DANGERS into SRAGEND, and 'eating' puts C after the S. Scrag end is a cheap British cut from the neck of mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag end is a cut of lamb or mutton from the neck, a type of butcher's cut.

clue.text: Festival always poetic taking place across a street

indicators.note: the poetic word spans the following letters, holding them inside

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A celebration that has always been held across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the Resurrection.
